definition: The act of moving a service component or release into one or more target environments.
rationale: Use this noun for the activity that moves a service component or release into a target environment, such as a test, staging, or live environment. It is not the release version or component set, the release-management practice, a change, an approval, an environment, a deployment tool or pipeline, or the service result after the move. Do not use it to mean that the release is available for use by service consumers.

allowed.text: The deployment moves the release to the staging environment before production use.
allowed.rationale: Names the movement activity, the release being moved, and the target environment.

not_allowed.text: The deployment is the version of the service made available to users.
not_allowed.rationale: Conflates the movement activity with the release version or component set.

criteria: Verify that the noun names moving a service component or release into one or more target environments.
Keep the noun distinct from a release version or component set, release-management practice, change, approval, environment, deployment tool or pipeline, and the post-deployment service result.
Confirm that the inspected PeopleCert page supports moving new or changed components to live, test, or staging environments but does not establish a complete universal ITIL glossary definition.
